title: Where Did This Value Come From: Settings from Four Places, Which One Wins, and the Typo That Was Silently Ignored

questions.question: A port is given on the command line as 9000 and in a config file as 8080, and the file is read after the arguments. Which does the program use?
options: 9000, if the settings rank their sources: the command line is meant more than a file, whatever order they are read in
questions.explanation: The suite measured 9000 from the command line.

questions.question: Why does each setting remember its source?
options: So a log can say log_level = debug (environment) and end the argument about which of four places set it

questions.question: speed_limt=0.5 is set and the robot goes at full speed. Why?
options: A map accepts any key and the program reads only those it knows, so a misspelt key just sits there
The limit is ignored on purpose
questions.explanation: unknown_keys found 5 of the 6 keys set.

questions.question: What is the edit distance between kitten and sitting?
options: 3: two letters changed and one added
questions.explanation: It counts single-character changes: a letter changed, left out or added.

questions.question: Why does prot for port count as two edits, not one?
options: A swap of two letters is two changes in this distance, one letter replaced and then the other
questions.explanation: The suggestion still found port, within two edits.

questions.question: LOG_LEVEL is set and log_level is known. What does suggest give, and why?
options: Nothing: the wrong case is eight edits, and a suggestion has to be within two
questions.explanation: A person is shown a suggestion, so a poor one is worse than none.
